title: Backstop constellation handoff and latency differential notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a conservative safety-lattice we want on the next mini-deploy (namespace: constellation-backfill). The goal is to define a small, operator-friendly handoff that catches small latency differentials early and provides deterministic backstop actions so SREs and on-call can move from observation to remediation without heavy Triage.

Quick summary:
- Deployment scope: constellation feature flag + kernel selector bump (v2.1.3 -> v2.2.0) on serving-runtime in eu-west-1 (canary cohort: 1%).
- Primary risk: small P95 latency drift (~10-25% increase) from kernel selector changes on longer context sequences (>2k tokens).
- Safety approach: two-tier backstop: soft throttle + traffic shepherding -> hard rollback if tail latency crosses step thresholds or error rate climbs.

Operational timeline (hourly block for 6h window):
- T-48h: Final smoke on staging with synthetic long-seq load (see test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tests/longseq-load). Confirm p95 < baseline + 5%.
- T-4h: Preflight checklist complete, on-call notified, incident channel created (#deploy-constellation-backstop).
- T-1h: Canary prepare: push canary config, reserve dedicated capacity lanes for backfill (ops ticket: JIRA-RELEASE-4123).
- T+0m: promote 1% of production traffic via canary routing policy. Watch first 5 minutes for obvious failures.
- T+15m: expand to 5% if checks pass.
- T+60m: (decision point) expand to 25% if p95 within thresholds and no sign of increased 5xx.
- T+180m: (final) expand to 100% if rolling metrics are nominal for the last 60 minutes at 25%.

Preflight checklist (quick pass to sign off):
- [ ] Smoke tests: staging longseq load green (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Canary config validated (route policy + capacity limits) (owner: Chen)
- [ ] Observability dashboards updated (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, qps slices) (owner: Sophie)
- [ ] Pager/alert tuning reviewed (doubling of 5xx or p95 > baseline + 20% triggers immediate action) (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Slack channel and incident playbook stub ready (#deploy-constellation-backstop) (owner: Aisha)

Signal definitions and decision grid (simple actionable rules):
- Primary signals: p95 latency (ms), 5xx rate (% of requests), user-facing error-rate (from frontend sampling).
- Supporting signals: CPU GPU saturation, KV cache hit rate, KV eviction spikes, tail token generation time, model-quant mismatch logs.

Decision grid (when to act):
- Alert level: VERBOSE WATCH: p95 > baseline + 10% sustained for 10m AND 5xx < 0.2% -> keep canary at current % and increase sampling/trace (owner: SRE on-call)
- Alert level: INTERVENTION: p95 > baseline + 20% OR 5xx >= 0.5% -> engage handoff (step-down described below). Notify eng-release-engineering and latency-owner channel.
- Alert level: EMERGENCY: p95 > baseline + 35% OR sustained growth in p99 OR user-facing errors spike > 0.75% -> immediate rollback to previous model/kernel and throttle new traffic.

Backstop actions (ordered, progressively stronger):
1) Increase tracing and sample more requests for top skewed paths (no customer impact).
2) Apply soft-throttle to feature (reduce canary traffic by 50%, reroute to stable kernel variant).
3) Shift traffic via traffic-shepherd to Dedicated capacity in adjacent region (eu-central-1) if latency is region-localized.
4) Disable kernel selector switch via feature flag (fast toggle) and revert to pinned kernel.
5) Hard rollback: reverse deploy (previous artifact) and re-run smoke. Notify customers if degradation persists > 30m.

Who does what (handoff matrix):
- SRE on-call (primary): initial alert triage, run checks, trigger soft-throttle, create incident doc.
- Release engineer (Aisha): coordinate decision grid escalation; authorize expansion beyond T+60m; own rollback if required.
- Serving runtime owner (Chen): patch kernel selection toggles and produce emergency patch if needed.
- Observability (Sophie): ensure dashboards show real-time slices, prepare a short telemetry snapshot for postmortem.
- Solutions/SEs: stand by for customer comm if they ping.

Communication templates (shortcuts to post in #deploy-constellation-backstop):
- Status (initial canary): "Canary deployed: constellation canary @ 1% in eu-west-1. Monitoring p95/p99, 5xx. Initial 5m checks in progress. Owners: @Aisha @Chen @SRE-oncall."
- Escalation: "Escalation: p95 exceeded threshold (X% over baseline) for 10m. Running soft-throttle -> reducing canary to Y%. Investigating traces."
- Rollback: "Rolling back constellation kernel selector (v2.2.0 -> v2.1.3). Redirecting canary traffic to stable lanes. Will update in ~10m with smoke results."

Telemetry and instrumentation notes (todo items):
- Add a short-lived span that tags requests hitting the new kernel selector so we can slice tail latency by path and input length. (Chen)
- Add synthetic user journey that exercises long-ctx generation every 5m and surfaces p95 anomalies in alerting. (Marco)
- Ensure token emission sampling logs include per-token time for the first 2k tokens to help detect drift. (Sophie)

Post-deploy checks and timeline for debrief:
- 0-3 hours after full promotion: hourly snapshot of p50/p95/p99 and error-rate. (SRE + Sophie)
- 24 hours: a clean postmortem note if any action beyond soft-throttle occurred. Include representative traces and sample payloads. (Aisha)
- 7 days: evaluate if kernel selector change should be reintroduced behind a more conservative quantization profile; feed into Optimize backlog.

Open questions / notes to self:
- If the latency differential is only visible for >3k token prompts, do we ship with an input-length cap temporarily? That reduces product utility but is an easy stopgap. Need product tradeoff decision.
- Confirm whether private deploy customers in the EU will see routing changes if traffic-shift to eu-central occurs. We may need a config guard.
- Run cost estimate for temporary Dedicated shift (rough estimate: +12% spend for 3 hours) and add as a parameter in release signoff.

Quick links and artifacts:
- Staging longseq harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tests/longseq-load
- Canary routing policy: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic/configs/constellation-canary.yaml
- Incident channel template: confluence.redwood/internal/deploy-guidelines#canary-incidents

Notes to the reader: this is intentionally concise. Use the decision grid as your primary operational contract during the canary. If any of the EMERGENCY criteria fire, prefer quick rollback over deep debugging in the first 30 minutes — we can collect traces and iterate after we stabilize traffic.

Annotated checklist (final pass for signoff):
- [ ] All preflight items done (timestamp and initials)
- [ ] Incident channel created and pinned message posted
- [ ] Canary monitor thresholds deployed to dashboards
- [ ] Owners and escalation ladder notified

-- Aisha (release engineer)
Last edits: 2026-03-15: tightened p95 thresholds, clarified synthetic harness link.
